(At Present Lodged In Central Jail Jodhpur)
 ----Petitioner  Versus State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp  ----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Vikas Vishnoi

For Respondent(s) : Mr. Javed Gauri, Dy.G.A.
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE FARJAND ALI Order 13/08/2024 1.
The jurisdiction of this court has been invoked by way of filing instant third bail application under Section 439 CrPC at the instance of accused-petitioner.

The requisite details of the matter are tabulated herein below:
S.No. Particulars of the Case  2. Concerned Police Station Mata-ka-than  3. District Jodhpur City East  4. Offences alleged in the FIR Section 363 of the IPC
5 . Offences added, if any Section 366, 376(2) of  the IPC and Section 5(l)/6  of the POCSO Act  6.

Date of passing of impugned 15.04.2024  order Gopal vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:34340) on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68127247/
1 2.
His first and second bail applications being SBCRLMB Nos.1956/2024 & 5013/2024 were dismissed as not pressed by this Court vide orders dated 20.03.2024 & 30.05.2024.

While [2024:RJ-JD:34340] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-9648/2024] dismissing the second bail application, this Court has afforded liberty to the petitioner to renew his prayer for bail after the recording the statement of victim.
Now the statement of victim has been recorded, hence, the instant bail application.

3. It is contended on behalf of the accused-petitioner that the relations between the petitioner and the victim were consensual thus no case for the alleged offences is made out against him and his incarceration is not warranted.
There are no factors at play in the case at hand that may work against grant of bail to the accused-petitioner and he has been made an accused based on conjectures and surmises.

4. Contrary to the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the bail application and submits that the present case is not fit for enlargement of accused on bail.
5. I have heard and considered the submissions made by both the parties and perused the material as made available to this Court.

6. Perusal of the material available on record, more particularly, the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. revealing that the relationship between her and petitioner were consensual.
She went the petitioner at her own free will and stayed with him at various places for about a month.
During the said period, both used public transportation but no alarm has been raised by her at any point of time.
FIR in this regard has been lodged after a month of the incident for which no satisfactory explanation for inordinate delay has been furnished.

After going [2024:RJ-JD:34340] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-9648/2024] through the allegations, as levelled in the FIR and her statements recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C. it is felt that there is a force in the defence submission that the relations between the victim and the petitioner were consensual and she was in agreement with the petitioner.
Looking to the high probability that the trial may take long time to conclude this Court deems it suitable to grant the benefit of bail to the petitioner.
7. It is nigh well settled law that at a pre-conviction stage; bail is a rule and denial from the same should be an exception.
The purpose behind keeping an accused behind the bars during trial would be to secure his presence on the day of conviction so that he may receive the sentence as would be awarded to him.
Otherwise, it is the rule of Crimnal Jurisprudence that he shall be presumed innocent until the guilt is proved.

8. Accordingly, the instant 3rd bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is ordered that the accused-petitioner as named in the cause title shall be enlarged on bail provided he furnishes a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned trial Judge for his appearance before the court concerned on all the dates of hearing as and when called upon to do so.
